entry.lemma: single-site lexical, syntactic and text-critical decisions of Isaiah 17
entry.partOfSpeech: mixed (nouns, construct chains, participles, a Pilpel verb, place names)
entry.literal: ruin(?), a fallen heap; the cities of Aroer; and the remnant of Aram, like the glory of; the glory of Jacob; harvest; the valley of Rephaim; in her branches, the fruitful one; the thicket and the treetop; the cities of his stronghold; plantings of pleasantness; a shoot of a stranger; you make grow(?); a heap of harvest; sick / inheritance; tumult … roar; wheel, whirl; storm-wind; he is not; our plunderers
entry.standardEnglish: ASV: 'a ruinous heap', 'The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down', 'and the remnant of Syria; they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel', 'the harvestman', 'in the outmost branches of a fruitful tree', 'the forsaken places in the wood and on the mountain top', 'pleasant plants … strange slips', 'thou hedgest it in … the harvest fleeth away in the day of grief', 'the whirling dust before the storm', 'them that rob us'. JPS 1917: 'make it to grow', 'A heap of boughs', 'plants of pleasantness … slips of a stranger'. NJPS: 'the mass of Israelites', 'tumbleweed before a gale', 'a delightful sapling … a disappointing slip', 'you see it grow … the branches wither away'. KJV: 'the harvest shall be a heap'. (ASV, KJV via bible-api.com; JPS 1917 and NJPS 1985 via Sefaria API v3; checked 2026-11-26.)
entry.wohChoice: 17:1 'a ruinous heap' (MT mᵉʿî as a by-form of ʿî; the lᵉʿî / dittography conjecture in commentary). 17:2 MT 'The cities of Aroer are forsaken' (the LXX-based emendation 'forsaken for ever' in commentary); wᵉrāḇᵉṣû rendered as a relative clause, 'which shall lie down' (ASV, JPS 1917), so that the masculine verb is referred to the flocks and not to the feminine cities (post-review refinement). 17:3 the accentual construal 'and the remnant of Aram; they shall be like the glory of the children of Israel' (ASV), with the JPS 1917 / NJPS subject reading in commentary. 17:3-4 kāḇôḏ 'glory' (strict wave concordance; NJPS 'mass' and the weight sense in commentary). 17:5 qāṣîr 'the harvester' (ASV 'harvestman', NJPS 'reaper'); ʿēmeq rᵉp̄āʾîm 'the valley of Rephaim', a place name, with the overlay rephaim-shades-dead-isaiah-26 and the central refaim-giant-peoples deliberately NOT applied. 17:6 'in the branches of the fruitful tree' (JPS 1917; ASV's added 'outmost' dropped). 17:9 MT 'the wood and the mountain top' (ASV), with the LXX 'Amorites and Hivites' in commentary; ʾāmîr 'mountain top' here against 'uppermost bough' at 17:6 (recorded departure: the image moves from tree to landscape); 'their strong cities' (ASV, NJPS) for the singular suffix. 17:10 'pleasant plants … strange slips' (ASV); the Adonis-gardens reading of naʿămānîm reported in a labelled comparative paragraph only, and the central dumuzi-tammuz-adonis-dying-and-rising-vegetation-god-cross-corpus deliberately NOT applied, since the line names no god. 17:11 tᵉśaḡśēḡî 'you make it grow' (JPS 1917, KJV, NJPS; ASV 'hedgest it in' in commentary); nēḏ qāṣîr 'the harvest shall be a heap' (MT pointing, KJV, JPS 1917; ASV 'fleeth away' and NJPS 'wither away' in commentary); naḥălāh 'grief' (Niphal participle of ḥlh). 17:12 root repetition kept, 'uproar … roar … roaring', 'rushing … rush … rushing' (ASV). 17:13 galgal 'whirling dust' (ASV, JPS 1917); sûp̄āh 'storm' here against 'whirlwind' at 5:28 and 29:6 (recorded departure); the singular bô rendered 'them'. 17:14 singular ʾênennû rendered 'they are no more' (ASV); bzz 'plunder', as at 10:2, 6; 13:16; 24:3.
entry.rationale: Each item is a site the Translator flagged where the Hebrew is rare, obscure or open to two construals. The Editor keeps the Masoretic text and a standard public-domain rendering in every line, and the commentary reports the alternatives with their sources. Two items in 17:11 change the Translator's ASV wording, and each follows a reference version. (a) The Pilpel tᵉśaḡśēḡî stands in synonymous parallel with taprîḥî 'you make blossom'. JPS 1917, KJV and NJPS read 'make grow'; ASV alone derives it from śûḡ 'fence about'. (b) As pointed, nēḏ is the noun 'heap' (Exod 15:8; Josh 3:13, 16; Ps 33:7; 78:13), which KJV and JPS 1917 follow. The verb nwd, read by ASV and NJPS, would normally give nāḏ, so keeping the pointing applies mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah. Two items depart from a concordance default, and the reasons are recorded here. At 17:9, ʾāmîr follows ASV 'mountain top' because the image there is a landscape of abandoned sites (NJPS treats both nouns as names). At 17:13, sûp̄āh keeps ASV 'storm', so that 'whirling dust before the whirlwind' is avoided; the concordance rules make only kāḇôḏ 'glory' strict. At 17:3 the accents (athnach on ʾărām) support ASV's construal, and JPS 1917 and NJPS's subject reading gives the same sense. At 17:5 the toponym is kept apart from the common noun rᵉp̄āʾîm 'shades / giants', because Josh 15:8 and 2 Sam 5:18, 22 locate a valley of that name near Jerusalem. At 17:10 the reading 'plantings of Adonis' is a history-of-religions hypothesis held by several commentators. The Hebrew names no god, and ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all render the adjective, so it belongs in labelled commentary and not in the line or the glossaryRefs. No item adopts a Wheel of Heaven reading, so the claim type is direct. Post-review refinement at 17:2: the Hebrew separates the feminine tihyeynāh (the cities) from the masculine wᵉrāḇᵉṣû (the flocks), so the line takes ASV and JPS 1917's 'which shall lie down' instead of 'and they shall lie down', which blurred the referent.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-4 (17:1): maśśāʾ dammāśeq 'The oracle concerning Damascus', as at 13:1 and 15:1. ASV and JPS 1917 'The burden of Damascus'; NJPS 'The "Damascus" Pronouncement' (Sefaria API v3, checked 2026-11-26).
Wave I-4 (17:1-3): 'Damascus' for the city (17:1, 3) and 'Aram' for the state in ûšᵉʾār ʾărām 'the remnant of Aram' (17:3), against ASV 'the remnant of Syria'. JPS 1917 and NJPS have 'Aram'.

Wave I-4: chapter 17 title 'Isaiah 17 — The oracle concerning Damascus: the thinning of Jacob's glory, the pleasant plants, and the roaring of the peoples' (the Translator's descriptive title, ratified; no lens).

Wave I-4: 17:6 nᵉʾum YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'says YHWH, the God of Israel'. At 17:10 the same rule governs the construct epithet ʾĕlōhê yišʿēḵ 'the God of your salvation' (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS 'the God who saves you'): a construct divine epithet is 'the God of …', and the Genesis 'the Elohim' convention is not applied.

Wave I-4: 17:7 yišʿeh hāʾāḏām ʿal-ʿōśēhû 'humankind shall look to their Maker'. The pronoun rule continues into 17:8, where hāʾāḏām is still the subject of the singular verbs and suffixes ('they shall not look … the work of their hands … their fingers'). ASV and NJPS have 'men … their', and JPS 1917 'a man … his' (Sefaria API v3 and bible-api.com, checked 2026-11-26).

Wave I-4: the lexical decisions of this entry, ʾăšērîm 'Asherim' and ḥammānîm 'sun-pillars', also govern 17:8, wᵉhāʾăšērîm wᵉhāḥammānîm 'the Asherim and the sun-pillars'. ASV and JPS 1917 have 'the Asherim, or the sun-images'. Correction for citation: NJPS at 17:8 reads 'sacred posts and incense stands', and at 27:9 'sacred post … incense altar' (Sefaria API v3, checked 2026-11-26). The central athirat-asherah-mother-goddess-cross-corpus-ugaritic-hebrew-bible is again not applied, because the referent is the cult object.

Wave I-4: the lower-case 'rock' for ṣûr as a divine epithet also governs 17:10, ṣûr māʿuzzēḵ 'the rock of your stronghold' (ASV 'the rock of thy strength'; JPS 1917 'the Rock of thy stronghold'; NJPS 'the Rock who shelters you'). The Yāh clause of this entry does not apply there.

Wave I-4: māʿôz is 'stronghold' at 17:10, ṣûr māʿuzzēḵ 'the rock of your stronghold' (JPS 1917 'stronghold'; ASV 'strength'). Context clause: in the construct chain ʿārê māʿuzzô (17:9), the noun is rendered adjectivally, 'strong cities' (ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS 'fortress cities'). The echo between 17:9 and 17:10 is pointed out in commentary. This entry's 'refuge / peace' clause does not apply in chapter 17.
Wave I-4: 17:12 is vocative, 'Woe, the uproar of many peoples' (ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS 'Ah'; KJV 'Woe to').

Wave I-4 (chapter 17 has no ketiv/qere): MT is kept against variants and emendations reported in commentary. These are: 17:2 the LXX-supported emendation 'forsaken for ever'; 17:3 the emendation of 'Ephraim' to 'Aram'; 17:9 the LXX 'the Amorites and the Hivites'; 17:10 the Vulgate-supported 'true' for naʿămānîm. Each is reported in NJPS's notes (Sefaria API v3, checked 2026-11-26), and the LXX and Vulgate texts themselves were not checked. At 17:11 the Masoretic pointing nēḏ 'heap' is kept against the reading nāḏ 'flees' of ASV and NJPS.
